entries.new_question: At the end of the preparation turn, is the body weight mainly over the back foot, between the feet, or over the front foot?
entries.reason: B's cause is rushing onto the front foot instead of 'turning over your outside foot' during preparation, which is visible; OBS-13 only covers weight at and after contact, and A's listed quotes (shoulder loading, racket roll, pro elbow path) do not support A's hip-coil text.

A ties the fault to striking the ball after the wrist is 'back to neutral' in the rolling follow-through (wrist motion through contact), while B's texts and quotes concern pulling close to vs 'farther away from your body' and make no wrist claim, so OBS-24 separates them only to the extent that B shows a stable wrist, which the material does not state.

Both describe the ball being taken too low ('far away from eye level' / 'the ball is just a little too low') and differ only in why it fails, harder perception of depth and timing vs the racket angle sending the ball 'down into the net', which a camera cannot separate when the visible contact is the same.
'Without this left hand supporting the racket down to here' and 'instead of just taking the left hand off coming to the pull slot' describe the same early release of the non-hitting hand.

A 'start with their shoulders level ... take your off shoulder and swing it higher' and B 'Keeping shoulders level ... prevents spinal side bend' describe the same missing shoulder tilt; B narrows it to low balls.
Rotating 'on a flat horizontal plane' without the off-shoulder rising and 'without allowing yourself to side bend on the way forward' are the same lack of trunk tilt into contact.
'Prevents spinal side bend' and 'lacks spine side bending on the way forward' name the same thing; A adds its downstream effect (elbow 'leaking down', 'very army' swing).

By text both are the absence of a hip hinge ('fails to hinge at the hips' vs 'rather than maintaining a hip hinge'), but none of B's listed quotes (aPcKJDadzek:Q01/Q05/Q23, uJpuDUx0jIA:Q01) mention hinging, so B's side has no quote support.

Both describe the same missing lower-body posture ('hinge at the hips' vs 'hip tilt, knee bend', 'I'm not really doing any of the things I just said'); B only adds a reason (predictable feeds) that is not itself visible.
By text both are the missing hip hinge or tilt ('rather than maintaining a hip hinge' vs 'do not require hip tilt'); A's listed quotes do not mention hinging, so A's side has no quote support.

Both show the same visible result (a 'really, really wristy' break), and the difference lies in muscle engagement ('the right hand providing the driving vector' vs 'at least a little bit of forearm tension'), which a camera cannot show.

'Adjust to low contact using the hand alone rather than bending at the knee and hip' and 'far below their eye level without bending their knees and hips' are the same failure to lower the body for low balls; B is stated for volleys.
